Roma’s transfer window will soon be in full swing.

Negotiations will be green-lit in January, but discussions are beginning in Trigoria about the next steps.

Gian Piero Gasperini wants an attacking winger and a fifth man: the budget available to Tony D’Amico to satisfy the Giallorossi coach remains to be determined.

And to raise funds, there’s Devyne Rensch, who hasn’t scored or provided any assists this season. The Dutchman could end up on the market.

According to recent reports, the club is savoring the capital gain with the No. 2: the player arrived in January 2025 for a total fee of €6 million, including fixed fee and bonuses. Should he leave, the Roman club will have to pay Ajax 10% of the difference between the selling price and the signing fee.

In addition to the capital gains glitch, which is not a priority for the Friedkins, Rensch could also leave the capital due to the repeated injuries that have kept him sidelined. His first injury problem with the Giallorossi dates back to February 2025, when the defender was sidelined for two matches. In total, the winger has missed 12 games in the capital since his arrival due to muscle problems, and is still out today.

Devyne was expected to return to the squad for the European away match against PSG, but that was not to be: after the first-degree injury he suffered during the match against Manchester United, the number 2 suffered a medium-grade tear to the adductor longus in his left leg. The 2003-born defender is targeting the match against Juventus on December 19th.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, bayern Munich are facing a huge blow with Harry Kane’s injury. The English striker seriously injured his left ankle during the match against Cologne (1-1) on Friday evening in the Bundesliga. Hit after contact with Joël Schmied, the 33-year-old striker was forced to leave his partners in the 20th minute. A premature exit which immediately aroused concern among the Bavarian staff. The medical examinations carried out subsequently unfortunately confirmed the fears of the Rekordmeister, who will have to do without his main offensive asset, recent winner of the 2026 Ballon d’Or, during a particularly notable period of the season.

The diagnosis is particularly difficult since Harry Kane suffers from a rupture of the syndesmotic ligament in his left ankle. Bayern Munich made the news official in a press release published Friday evening. “Harry Kane tore the syndesmotic ligament in his left ankle during Bayern’s home Bundesliga match against Cologne on Friday evening. This was revealed by an examination carried out by the FC Bayern medical department. The 33-year-old will therefore be absent from the field for the next few months.announced the German club. A significant unavailability which deprives Vincent Kompany of his starting center forward for several major deadlines. With a busy schedule and high ambitions on the European scene, Bayern must now consider solutions to compensate for this absence during the winter transfer window.

It has been revealed that the Bavarian management is starting to seriously look at the transfer market. According to information from Bildsupplemented by La Gazzetta dello Sportseveral profiles are being studied with a view to the next winter transfer window. The Nicolò Tresoldi track particularly attracts attention. The 22-year-old center forward plays for Club Bruges and has established himself as one of the most coveted young attackers on the continent. A German international hopeful, he is at the heart of a sporting battle with Italy, who are also seeking to attract him to their ranks. His performances in Belgium have already attracted several European teams, including AC Milan. Bayern could therefore enter into particularly strong competition to secure his services. Club Brugge would have set its demands at 60 million euros, a significant amount for an operation envisaged from January. The list of possibilities does not end at Tresoldi.

According to the transalpine newspaper, Bayern is also following Ricardo Pepi, former Augsburg striker now at PSV Eindhoven, as well as Igor Thiago, who plays at Brentford. For his part, Bild has put forward the name of Younes Ebnoutalib, the 23-year-old Eintracht Frankfurt striker. Revelation of the season, he scored eight goals in twelve matches and enjoys growing popularity in Germany. The daily newspaper mentions a player appreciated by Jürgen Klopp and compared internally to the young Robert Lewandowski. Paris Brunner is among the profiles mentioned. The former great hope of Borussia Dortmund is now playing in Monaco, where he continues his progress. His younger profile and his potential could represent a different alternative for Munich’s leaders. On the Rock, the Italian press mentions the Folarin Balogun file which is still monitored by Bavarian leaders, while Sky Sport Germany talks about a possible return of Eric Maxim Choupo-Moting, free agent in a few months. So many avenues which testify to the reflection undertaken in Bavaria, even if no official decision has been confirmed concerning winter recruitment.

  • The Real Madrid striker faced Celta de Vigo this Saturday and provided an assist in a 2-1 success.
  • Fourth, Dušan Vlahović continues to shine in Türkiye.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that this Monday is the ninth report in the ranking of European top scorers for the 2026/2027 season. We thus find the scorers who shook the nets in Germany, England, Belgium, Spain, France, Italy, Netherlands, Portugal and Türkiye. And as since the start of the season, Raphinha takes the lead. Mute against Villarreal during a 3-2 victory with the Catalan club, the Brazilian has 15 goals in 12 matches.

Just behind, we find Kylian Mbappé. The Real Madrid striker faced Celta de Vigo this Saturday and provided an assist in a 2-1 success. Not scoring during this match, the French striker has 13 goals in 13 matches. The podium is completed by Donyell Malen. The Dutch striker walks on water with AS Roma. Against Parma this Saturday, he scored a quadruple and brought his tally to 12 goals in 11 matches.

Fourth, Dušan Vlahović continues to shine in Türkiye. The Serbian striker bagged a brace against Konyaspor in a 4-2 win with Besiktas. Here he is now credited with 11 goals in 10 matches. Vangelis Pavlidis comes fifth with 11 goals in 11 matches. The Greek did not play in the league since Benfica beat Torreense in the Portuguese Cup (3-1). Sixth, Yassir Zabiri impresses in La Liga with 11 goals in 13 matches. The Moroccan scored a double with Racing Santander in the 3-2 success against Real Sociedad.

In a recent development, niclas Füllkrug comes seventh with 10 goals in 10 matches and scored a upcoming pawn with Werder Bremen against Hamburg (4-0). He is thus ahead of Gift Orban who was silent during Amedspor’s 2-0 loss against Rizespor. Ninth, Nicolo Tresoldi maintains the pace with 10 goals in 12 matches. The Bruges striker remains on a double against Mechelen (5-1). Finally, Lamine Yamal completes the ranking even if he did not score against Villarreal in a 3-2 victory.

It has been revealed that victor Osimhen (Galatasaray), Sven Mijnans (PSV Eindhoven), Gustavo Varela (Monza), Erling Haaland (Manchester City), Patrik Schick (Bayer Leverkusen), Lassine Sinayoko (Paris FC), Søren Tengstedt (Go Ahead Eagles), Thom van Bergen (Groningen), Brynjólfur Willumsson (Groningen), Wout Weghorst (Twente), Mohamed Salah (Trabzonspor), Luis Suárez (Sporting CP) and Adrian Benedyczak (Kasimpasa) failed to reach the top 10 with 9 goals. Amine Gouiri (Olympique de Marseille), Norman Bassette (Westerlo), Dennis Eckert (Standard de Liège), Eldor Shomurodov (Başakşehir), Antonio Raimondo (Frosinone) and Ante Budimir (Osasuna) follow with 8 goals.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that long chains of sugars known as polysaccharides support many biological functions, from strengthening tissues to modulating cell signalling. Synthesizing these compounds in the laboratory with precise lengths and architectures, which are needed to establish how the structures of polysaccharides affect biological behaviour, has been difficult. Writing in Nature, Yin et al.1 now report an enzyme-based strategy that produces highly uniform polysaccharides and enables chains to restart growth after consuming all of the sugar building blocks in the reaction, once more sugars are added. The authors achieved this control by adjusting how readily an enzyme binds the small sugar molecules that are used to initiate the growth of each chain.

Hapless, hopeless and utterly humiliated. And that has to be that for Michael Carrick. It is surely inconceivable that he will continue any longer as Manchester United’s head coach. A proud club on its knees and a favoured son on his way out.

They are 14 points off the top already, but forget that. It is irrelevant given their plight.

It has been revealed that that is how far United have, once again, fallen. Fans in the Stretford End unfurled their “Standards” banner, bearing the faces of Eric Cantona, Roy Keane and Bryan Robson.

In a recent development, it was first revealed in December 2021 in Carrick’s final match as interim following Ole Gunnar Solskjaer’s sacking. This should be his final game again, under different, more traumatic, circumstances.

According to recent reports, if it is, he is going out having made a stand. He dropped Bruno Fernandes for his outspoken comments, aimed directly at Carrick and his tactics, following the dismal 4-1 Champions League defeat away to Como on Wednesday.

Welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of Manchester United vs Bouremouth.

United enter Sunday’s clash against Bournemouth in the grip of a deepening crisis. Wednesday night’s dismal 4-1 Champions League defeat to debutants Como extended United’s’ winless run to seven matches across all competitions - their worst sequence since 2015.

Recent findings suggest that with just one victory from their opening seven Premier League fixtures, United are enduring their worst start to a top-flight season since 1986-87. Head coach Michael Carrick, a multiple champion at Old Trafford during his playing days, finds his position under severe threat, with reports suggesting another defeat could seal his departure. While both of United’s wins this season have come at home, they remain winless in their last three at Old Trafford. On an individual level, Bryan Mbeumo has offered a rare bright spark, scoring four goals in seven league outings while Bruno Fernandes continues to search for form, and the captain’s recent outburst only makes the atmosphere more febrile.

According to recent reports, in stark contrast, Bournemouth arrive in Manchester brimming with confidence. Marco Rose’s side have enjoyed a flawless start to their inaugural European campaign, sitting joint-top of the Europa League standings after a dominant 3-0 victory over Ruben Amorim’s ten-man AC Milan on Thursday. That result marked a third consecutive home win and clean sheet, with Bournemouth outscoring opponents 8-0 in that stretch. Midfielder Marcus Tavernier has been instrumental, leading the club’s scoring charts with five goals across 11 appearances.

Bournemouth will feel no trepidation visiting Old Trafford, having gone unbeaten in their last six Premier League meetings with United (two wins, four draws). With Carrick desperate for a stabilising result and Rose’s side riding high on European momentum, today’s fixture carries significant stakes for both clubs.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

José Mourinho had a lot to say after Real Madrid’s stunning victory over Celta Vigo. Jostled by the Galicians, the Merengues had to fight to snatch a precious success thanks to Bellingham and Carlos Espi. A more complicated meeting than expected for the Portuguese technician, who notably pointed out the fatigue of his internationals and the lack of concentration of his team at the start of the match. But at the press conference, the Special One especially put on a show when discussing his offensive choices. Asked about Carlos Espí, who continues to be decisive despite limited playing time, Mourinho explained at length the qualities of his striker. “He’s a surface player. When you dominate an opponent who is content to defend, his game is devastating. He has quality in the area, he plays with his back to goal, he is good with his head, he attacks both posts… He has all the qualities of an area player. History is full of players like him, decisive even with limited playing time”he remarked.

Sources indicate that and Mourinho was keen to underline the impeccable state of mind of his player, who does not seem disturbed by his status in the Madrid offensive hierarchy. “We are happy with him. He’s the kind of player who doesn’t get distracted by discussions about his playing time: Should Kylian be a substitute or play more? He knows that he is progressing, that he has the respect of the coach, his teammates and the supporters. He is happy. And I hope to have the opportunity to give him tenure, 90 minutes or more”continued the Portuguese. A way of also justifying the use and playing time of Carlos Espi with a Madrid team rather focused on offensive transitions and depth.

It has been revealed that but the José Mourinho show really began when a journalist asked him if he was considering combining Kylian Mbappé and Carlos Espí at the forefront of his attack. A possibility that Mourinho does not completely rule out, but which would pose serious balance problems for his team. And the Portuguese technician found a rather original way of explaining it. “I can do it, but when we lose the ball, I, being on the sideline, will have to enter the field in transition and punch someone to stop the counter-attack! Because playing with two pure strikers means the wingers have to defend inside. And it will certainly not be Diomandé, Vinicius, Arda… A little Brahim, perhaps. But with the characteristics of our wingers, we are not made to play in a classic 4-4-2”he stated. Behind the joke, Mourinho insisted on the tactical constraints of such an association. “It’s more complicated than you might think. It’s easier for the supporters, as well as for you. But the reality is a little more difficult. ».

According to recent reports, finally, José Mourinho also took advantage of this press conference to end the suspense concerning Vinicius Junior. While questions surrounded the presence of the Brazilian in the starting lineup during the next meeting in Madrid with his goals for Brazil during the break, the Special One preferred to cut short speculation with his usual humor. “I said it yesterday, it doesn’t matter whether he’s a substitute or a starter. To avoid you asking me the question on Monday and having too much to say, I’m going to be a bad boy and end the story: he will start Tuesday in the Champions League.he announced. An answer which has the merit of being clear, while Mourinho wants to juggle and alternate between offensive positions. And after a difficult victory against Celta Vigo, the Madrid coach recalled that at Real Madrid, aligning all the offensive talents was not necessarily enough to build a balanced team.

Published: 03:30 EST, 26 November 2026 | Updated: 05:12 EST, 26 November 2026.

When England and Manchester United defender Harry Maguire finally decides to hang up his boots, he may have an alternative to the pundits’ studio.

Maguire, 33, is co-founder of a latest AI coaching app, Feedz, that is already transforming the way elite sports teams are instructing their talent with their cutting-edge voice-to-report technology.

The Manchester United centre-half started the company alongside British tech entrepreneur Matt White in May and the app is already being used by sporting outfits, including Maguire's club United, Chelsea's women's team and Sunderland.

Having bounced back from setbacks and criticism throughout his career, Maguire's resilience will stand him in good stead if he decides to transition from the backline to the touchline.

And while it is not a traditional managerial role his decision demonstrates a keen eye on the future of coaching and the development of young athletes.

A lot of latest AI developments are mind-boggling on the face of it, but what sets Feedz apart is just how easy it is to use.

Harry Maguire has co-founded the revolutionary upcoming AI coaching app, Feedz.

All a coach needs to do is dictate a messy audio message giving instructions to a player and within seconds Feedz will provide them with a PDF outlining exactly where their player is succeeding, where they must improve and how to do it.

Even more impressive, the use of this app is not limited to football and indeed has fast become a tool used all over the globe in 19 different sports.

Feedz has also been able to cross the Atlantic, with the technology being used by a plethora of elite institutions across the pond – most notably Sporting Jacksonville, who, with more than 150 coaches training 10,000 young players, are the largest soccer academy in the States and something of a feeder club for top MLS teams.

Co-founder Matt White tells Daily Mail Sport: 'The purpose of Feedz is to develop youth sports. There is no downside to feedback, transparency between coach, player and parent is the flywheel.

Industry observers note that 'The issue is time. Coaches don’t have the time to give feedback consistently, the technology now exists to solve that problem of time. Coaches can now give feedback in seconds.

'This is across all sports. Caroline Elite, a US soccer academy in the US, have over 2,000 players... it used to take them two weeks to give feedback to these players and  now it takes two hours.'.

White then emphasised the vast number of sports in which Feedz can be used, and outlined the elite outfits already using it.

'Feedz is for all sports,' he indicates. 'Multiple schools, cricket counties like Surrey, Sussex, Kent, Glamorgan, Middlesex. Table Tennis England, Sale Sharks rugby club, Surbiton hockey club, Sunderland AFC, Manchester United, West Riding Oxfordshire (riding club), Louisiana Fire, Arizona Arsenal, Sporting Iowa (US soccer teams), Soccer Indiana. They all use Feedz.

Recent findings suggest that 'Good feedback helps a young player understand what they’re doing well and what to work on. It also helps parents feel involved and gives coaches a way to track progress over time.'.

Another encouraging aspect of Feedz is that the firm aims to help young sportspeople at all levels of the game.

White explains that when he started the organization he went straight to the FA's head of grassroots football to ensure that coaches who simply don't have the time or resources to relay meaningful feedback to their players could do so.

His savvy investment may point to Maguire's intends post-retirement.

He went on to explain that at the highest level professional athletes have nutritionists, personal physios and all of the available data handed to them to ensure they can perform at their best but young talent are often not given the same chance to reach their potential.

Maguire told White: 'This is the exact kind of thing I would have loved to have as a young player coming through.'.

In a world where the majority of stories on AI are negative and inspire fear, this is a use of the technology that can keep grassroots football alive and even help it thrive.

And, just as he approaches the twilight of his own career, Maguire clearly agrees.

For several weeks already, his fate had been sealed. Michael Carrick was finally dismissed from his position this Thursday, after meeting his now ex-leaders the same morning. Omar Berrada, the general manager, and Jason Wilcox, the football director, informed him of the end of the adventure, three days after the announcement of his imminent departure. It is this method that is being singled out today by the press and observers, more than the dismissal of the Manchester United coach. The situation was becoming inevitable.

Sources indicate that while he knew he was doomed since Monday morning, the day after the draw at Old Trafford against Aston Villa (4-4), the technician continued his mission, biding his time. His representatives had been contacted by management to announce their intentions to separate. Except that in the meantime, Berrada and Wilcox hopped on a plane to Monaco to meet the club’s co-owner, Sir Jim Ratcliffe, and finalize the details together. Only returning to Manchester on Wednesday evening, they then called Carrick to arrange a meeting the following morning.

Sources indicate that according to The Telegraphthis way of doing things and this very long wait upset the former midfielder. He did not understand why he had to organize the sessions on Tuesday and Wednesday, without most of the management players, who had left for selection, but with his assistants: Steve Holland, Jonathan Woodgate, Jonny Evans and Travis Binnion, all fired since yesterday. At the same time, MU was working on the arrival of Mauricio Pochettino. In this tense context, made of mutual reproaches and delaying tactics, the information inevitably leaked.

According to recent reports, “Over the past 24 to 48 hours, the situation has been catastrophic. While the manager, a club legend, directs training on the field, the management and owner are in Monaco, and simultaneously contact the American Football Federation to approach Mauricio Pochettino», jumps Gary Neville in the still very popular podcast, Stick to Football by The Overlap. “It’s simply sickening. This is well below the standards expected in any other company, in any other industry. This would be unfair dismissal and you would be prosecuted», Continues the former Mancunian defender.

“Being in Monaco while the team, the staff and the people who manage the club on a daily basis are in Manchester is very frowned upon, and it casts a negative light on the management. I don’t think anyone will come out of this unscathed.» Strong words which echo those made the day before by Peter Schmeichel, another legend of the Red Devils of the 90s. «If they look for someone else, let them relieve him of his duties! Don’t let him come and lead the training. He did it again yesterday (Wednesday). How disrespectful is that?», asked the former goalkeeper.

It has been revealed that faced with Carrick’s anger, management tried to defend itself, again according to The Telegraph. She understands the frustration of the 45-year-old technician and regrets that their separation happened like this. She also denies having carried out all the checks (notably legal) prior to and necessary for dismissal, before communicating her decision to the person concerned. The club believes it has demonstrated all possible transparency. These explanations will not convince many people as Manchester United is used to these procedures. The dismissal of Amorim, for example, is less than a year old….

Intelligent women get less help at work, study finds

📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (726 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • High intelligence is usually counted as an asset at work.
  • In a recent development, across 826 people in the United States and China, women who scored higher on an intelligence test were rated by their teammates as more hostile, received less help and were undermined more often.
  • The study examined whether people's cognitive ability affects how their teammates treat them and whether that differs between women and men.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

High intelligence is usually counted as an asset at work. But a new study suggests that for women, it can also lead to worse treatment from colleagues.

In a recent development, across 826 people in the United States and China, women who scored higher on an intelligence test were rated by their teammates as more hostile, received less help and were undermined more often. Men with high scores did not receive such treatment, and in one group, they were treated better.

The study examined whether people's cognitive ability affects how their teammates treat them and whether that differs between women and men.

It has been revealed that since it was published this year, Nitya Chawla, an associate professor at UCL School of Management in London and the researcher behind the study, notes women have written to her saying the findings matched their own experience at work. Some told her they had wondered whether they were to blame for hostility.

Industry observers note that the researchers ran two studies. The first followed 432 business students at a US public university working in small teams on a consulting project for real organizations. The second surveyed 394 full-time employees working in teams at a financial organization in China.

It has been revealed that intelligence here means cognitive ability measured with a standardized test of reasoning and problem-solving that employers use in hiring. Teammates were not told of anyone's scores. They rated one another, and a few weeks later each person reported how much help they had received and how often they had been undermined, for instance by having information withheld.

The effects were small, and the study demonstrates a link, not proof that colleagues' perceptions caused the treatment. Participants reported help and mistreatment themselves, and the study did not look at race or ethnicity.

In the student group, the difference between women and men was no longer statistically significant when two participants with extremely low scores were included.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Industry observers note that the researchers point to social role theory, the idea that people expect men and women to fit traditional roles: men as capable and assertive, women as warm and supportive. A woman with high cognitive ability breaks that expectation, and colleagues may assume she lacks warmth.

"It's that automatic, implicit assumption that takes place alongside the presence of intelligence that then drives these more negative interpersonal behaviors," Chawla told DW.

In a recent development, in both groups, women with higher scores were rated as more hostile. Among the employees in China, they were also rated as less warm. Women seen as more hostile reported less help, both with their work and on a personal level, and more undermining.

Sources indicate that the team also checked whether the women were simply behaving differently. Higher-scoring women were rated as somewhat more domineering, but that did not explain why they received less help or more mistreatment. The findings point to colleagues' assumptions, Chawla indicates, rather than to anything the women did.

No, men with high intelligence scores do not face the same treatment. Among the students in the United States, a man's score made no difference to how his teammates rated or treated him.

Recent findings suggest that among the employees in China, men with higher scores were rated as less hostile, received more help and were mistreated less often. The authors suggest the difference between the two groups may reflect cultural differences in gender norms, but they did not test this.

No, Chawla claims. "That would be really the wrong conclusion to draw.".

Small effects still matter, she argues, because they are experienced day after day. Over time, this kind of treatment can lead to anxiety, self-doubt and a sense of not belonging. "These experiences and these feelings can become very, very burdensome over time," she said.

It has been revealed that chawla puts the responsibility on workplaces rather than on women. Managers, she says, should track how team members treat one another, and organizations should hold regular check-ins to see whether employees are getting equal support.

Individuals can ask themselves a simple question, she notes: would they react the same way if that colleague were a man?

This article is an excerpt from our podcast Science Unscripted.

  • According to information from Guardianconfirmed by RMC SportPhilippe Diallo could finally be the surprise candidate chosen by UEFA to challenge Gianni Infantino.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The race for the FIFA presidency is entering its home stretch. While Gianni Infantino intends to run for a upcoming mandate during the election scheduled for March 18, 2027 in Rabat, Morocco, the opponents of the outgoing president still have a few days to find a candidate capable of bringing their challenge. The deadline for submitting applications is set for November 18, i.e. Wednesday, and UEFA is working to present a profile likely to unite its 55 member associations. A delicate mission for the European body, which has been looking for several weeks for a sufficiently influential personality to embody a credible alternative. Meanwhile, the Italian-Swiss leader is increasing diplomatic trips and seduction operations with the various confederations to consolidate his lead, at a time when Kozo Tashima, honorary president of the Japanese Football Federation, is also a candidate.

However, the avenues have multiplied in recent weeks without really coming to fruition. As we revealed to you exclusively this morning, UEFA once considered supporting Luis Figo, with the idea of ​​banking on the notoriety of the former Portuguese international to lead the battle against the FIFA president. An option which was not ultimately unanimous within the European body. Other names have also been circulating, starting with that of Arsène Wenger, director of world football development at FIFA, whose possible candidacy would have required a spectacular change of position. The former Arsenal coach would have ultimately declined this possibility. Didier Drogba and Mikaël Silvestre were also mentioned, without these avenues materializing. Faced with these successive refusals and the urgency of the timetable, European leaders must now make their choice.

According to information from Guardianconfirmed by RMC SportPhilippe Diallo could finally be the surprise candidate chosen by UEFA to challenge Gianni Infantino. The president of the French Football Federation, in office since 2023, would have taken a step ahead of the other contenders and his candidacy could be made official on Tuesday. The UEFA executive committee must meet to examine this possibility and seek the approval of the 55 member federations. The choice of a French leader would mark a change in strategy for Europe, which initially hoped to rely on a personality with greater international notoriety, from the field or the sidelines. Philippe Diallo, however, presents the profile of an experienced administrator and has gradually established himself as one of the most assertive opponents of Infantino. Last September, he considered that the initiatives of the FIFA president during and after the 2026 World Cup had seriously damaged the image and unity of football, considering that trust was broken.

Sources indicate that it now remains to be seen whether this candidacy can really shake up Gianni Infantino who maintains a very favorable position. Philippe Diallo could count on the support of the vast majority of European associations, but also try to convince several French-speaking federations of the African Football Confederation. A job of persuasion which promises to be particularly complicated, since the outgoing president benefits from numerous relays on the African continent and in other confederations. According to RMC SportInfantino would already have 80 to 90 votes acquired from the votes expected in March 2027. Philippe Diallo’s lack of international notoriety also constitutes a serious handicap, despite his weight within French and European football. THE Guardian also underlines that the multiplication of opposing candidates could ultimately serve the interests of the outgoing president, who would have an easy time presenting himself as the candidate of unity in the face of a divided opposition. The possible appointment of the boss of the FFF would open a latest chapter in this political battle, without guaranteeing UEFA the ability to shake Gianni Infantino.

#220689. What are fossil fuels?

What are fossil fuels?

📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (597 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Whether in the form of crumbly rock, odorless gas or slick black liquid, ancient organic compounds have powered the flourishing of modern life.
  • The collective term refers to coal, oil and natural gas — a group of energy sources that contain carbon and hydrogen.
  • They started life hundreds of millions of years ago as living plants and animals.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Whether in the form of crumbly rock, odorless gas or slick black liquid, ancient organic compounds have powered the flourishing of modern life. But now they threaten to make the planet unlivable for many plants, animals and humans.

The collective term refers to coal, oil and natural gas — a group of energy sources that contain carbon and hydrogen.

They started life hundreds of millions of years ago as living plants and animals. When they died, they sank to the bottom of oceans and swamps where they decomposed under layers of sediment.

Over time, this matter was buried deeper and deeper into the earth, subjecting it to increasing pressure and heat which changed its chemical composition. Plants and trees transformed into coal, whereas microscopic plankton and algae became oil and — if the heat and pressure increased further — gas.

Today fossil fuels can be found in the earth's crust all around the world although some countries, such as the US, Saudi Arabia and Russia, have bigger reserves than others.

Coal, found in underground coal beds, is extracted by mining, whereas oil and gas, found in reservoirs beneath the land and ocean, are accessed by drilling.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Since the early 19th Century, when the discovery and exploitation of fossil fuel reserves powered the Industrial Revolution, our use of them has skyrocketed, increasing eight-fold since 1950.

Today they provide 80% of our energy needs through heating, electricity generation and transport.

We transform them into energy either by burning them directly in furnaces that warm up our homes and businesses, or in power plants to heat water into steam which then generates electricity. When it comes to transport, crude oil is refined into a range of products such as diesel, gasoline and kerosene that are burned in the engines of automobiles, airplanes and ships. Natural gas is also sometimes compressed for use in cars and buses.

But fossil fuels are also essential to a huge range of products including steel, formed using a coal-derived material called coke, and plastic, which is produced by refining and processing crude oil and gas.

Sources indicate that fossil fuels are by far the biggest contributors to climate change. When burned to power our modern lives, they emit carbon dioxide (CO2) into Earth's atmosphere, trapping heat and causing temperatures to rise.

With 2025 officially one of the warmest years on record, the impact of these emissions is being felt around the world. Hotter temperatures are causing polar ice caps to melt and creating the conditions for extreme weather events — such as floods, drought, wildfires and storms — to become more intense and frequent.

It has been revealed that scientists stress the need to limit global warming to 1.5 degrees Celsius (2.7 degrees Fahrenheit) to avoid unleashing the most catastrophic impacts of climate change. That was laid out in the 2015 Paris Agreement. At the moment, there are 194 parties to the agreement, but progress has been too slow, and overall emissions continue to rise.

In a recent development, three years after countries agreed at the UN climate conference in Dubai COP28 to transition away from coal, oil and gas. After the previous COP in Brazil failed to reach a consensus on a concrete proposal, Brazil has now presented a roadmap aimed at turning that promise into national intends.

"It is long past time to stop treating the transition away from fossil fuels as taboo or intractable," United Nations Secretary-General Antonio Guterres said.

Senne Lammens has NOT fully recovered from World Cup howler, claims Peter Schmeichel after Man United goalkeeper's nightmare in Lisbon - as Joshua Zirkzee insists squad will rally around under-fire team-mate

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (774 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By BEN WILLCOCKS, ASSISTANT SPORTS EDITOR and CHRIS WHEELER, NORTHERN SPORTS WRITER.
  • Published: 04:00 EST, 26 November 2026 | Updated: 06:54 EST, 26 November 2026.
  • Manchester United legend Peter Schmeichel fears Senne Lammens has yet to recover from the blunder he made during Belgium's World Cup campaign last summer.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By BEN WILLCOCKS, ASSISTANT SPORTS EDITOR and CHRIS WHEELER, NORTHERN SPORTS WRITER.

Published: 04:00 EST, 26 November 2026 | Updated: 06:54 EST, 26 November 2026.

Manchester United legend Peter Schmeichel fears Senne Lammens has yet to recover from the blunder he made during Belgium's World Cup campaign last summer.

Lammens made two costly mistakes in United’s 2-2 Champions League draw with Sporting Lisbon on Wednesday night, conceding a needless penalty and dropping a clanger in the dying minutes to allow Luis Suarez to score twice for the home side.

The 24-year-old goalkeeper, who was one of Manchester United's standout performers last season following his £18.1million transfer from Royal Antwerp, has looked unconvincing so far this term and played a part in the club conceding more goals (35) than any other side in Europe's top five leagues.

Former Red Devils goalkeeper Schmeichel believes Lammens has never fully recovered from his error that led to Belgium being dumped out by Spain at the World Cup quarter-final stage last summer.

In the 88th minute of the match, with the score locked at 1-1, Lammens spilled the ball into the path of Mikel Merino, who tapped home to send Spain through to the semi-finals.

Asked if the confidence-shot goalkeeper should now be dropped by Mauricio Pochettino for Karl Darlow, who was signed by United in the summer, Schmeichel told CBS Sports: ‘I don’t know where that point is.

Senne Lammens made two massive errors during Manchester United's 2-2 draw at Sporting Lisbon.

Peter Schmeichel fears Lammens has never fully recovered from his blunder at the World Cup.

‘Mauricio Pochettino has come in, he’s brought his own staff, that means he’s got a upcoming goalkeeping coach and maybe that is something that can change it for him.

‘I don’t know if you remember in the World Cup, he came against Spain and made a bit of a mistake, Merino scored and they got knocked out, and I feel like he’s lost a little bit of confidence from that mistake, hasn’t really recovered.

‘As a goalkeeper when you’re not on your best form you need your defenders in front of you to help you out and the sad truth is that they haven’t been able to do that and of course, that makes it so much worse.'.

Joshua Zirkzee insists United’s players will rally around Lammens and won’t let their under-fire goalkeeper ‘suffer by himself’.

The two costly errors undid Lammens’ good work after he saved an earlier penalty from Suarez, but Zirkzee stated the players are determined to support the Belgian.

‘This team is a family, so there's no one who will suffer by themselves,’ stated Zirkzee. ‘Mistakes happen. Let's go on to the next one. Senne’s a great goalkeeper.

‘In this moment, we just give him space. I’m not sure if he wants to hear anything at all. But Senne’s a great kid. He's got a good head on him and we all know that next game he is going to be at the top of his game. We didn't draw because of him. I'm also someone who likes to look at myself and, you know, I didn't score.’.

United had two goals disallowed by Polish referee Szymon Marciniak as well as conceding the two penalties and seeing Youri Tielemans sent off – three days after Leny Yoro was shown a controversial red card at Liverpool – and Zirkzee admitted that it feels like the world is against Pochettino’s team at the moment.

The Belgian shot-stopper conceded a needless penalty just minutes after saving a spot-kick.

He then spilled the ball into the path of Luis Suarez late on, gifting Sporting a late equaliser.

‘Yeah, we're in a place where it can feel like that pretty quick,’ he added. ‘But as I noted, we've got a locker-room that's built on supporting each other and we will get out of it eventually. If it's us against the world, so be it.

‘For the team that we are, we shouldn't really be looking at what the referee decides, but you cannot deny that it was some key decisions that weren't in our favour, to put it like that.

‘But, as I said, we shouldn't really be looking at the referee. All we have to do is look at ourselves. In the end, I think we drew because of small details, little mistakes. But we definitely have something to build on, mainly the way we started the second half. I think that's something we can build on and move on with. Our team should be capable to win even if we're not being favoured in those moments.’.

#220687. Celebrating Neil Warnock & his most infamous dressing room meltdown

Celebrating Neil Warnock & his most infamous dressing room meltdown

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (923 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Planetfootball

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • “The public perception of Neil Warnock is definitely different to the reality of what the guy is.”.
  • So says Shaun Derry, who played under Warnock at Crystal Palace and QPR and must know a thing or two about what makes the infamously irate manager tick.
  • The theme of split personalities crops up time and again when former players discuss their time with him.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

“The public perception of Neil Warnock is definitely different to the reality of what the guy is.”.

So says Shaun Derry, who played under Warnock at Crystal Palace and QPR and must know a thing or two about what makes the infamously irate manager tick.

The theme of split personalities crops up time and again when former players discuss their time with him. Away from football, Colin Neil is portrayed as a laid-back guy, enjoying the tech giant of his family down in Cornwall.

Warnock himself gifted us with this beautifully idyllic image: “I cut the grass and feed the ducks and listen to the birds singing,” he told Cornwall Live about his life during lockdown.

But simply watching Warnock during a football match is enough to raise your blood pressure.

Sources indicate that the veteran manager, arguably the most Yorkshire male in existence, doesn’t burden his players with complex tactical instructions. But he does expect his players to follow those instructions down to the last fuckin’ letter.

It’s at this point we should introduce Chris Morgan. A famously combative centre-back, Morgan was sent off six times for both Barnsley and Sheffield United, holding the record for red cards at both clubs.

In a recent development, if ever a player represented a manager on the pitch, it was Morgan under Warnock at Bramall Lane. And, to paraphrase Eminem, when a tornado meets a volcano you get explosive results. Explosive and hilarious results.

Sources indicate that years before Amazon premiered their ‘All or Nothing’ series, Warnock allowed the cameras to document Sheffield United’s 2004-05 season. We can only hope it was him that insisted on the final title – ‘Warnock’.

What must have seemed like a good idea at the time began to look ill-judged as the club’s push for the Premier League started to falter.

And the most iconic moment of a must-watch film came after a home match against Wolves in 2004.

Sources indicate that gotta laugh at archive Neil Warnock going at Chris Morgan back in the day! 😂.

🎥 Sky Sports pic.twitter.com/y8mB4OJlxb.

— Empire of the Kop (@empireofthekop) June 21, 2017.

Leading 3-2 against the pre-season promotion favourites, United conspired to allow Joleon Lescott to plunder a late equaliser. Not only had two points been dropped, but the mother of all fuses had been lit.

As the dejected Blades players re-entered the dressing room, Warnock stood waiting with hands on his hips and ready to ask the burning question: “Who’s got him?”.

Phil Jagielka, wearing what appears to be a Selkirk Rex on his head, began to protest his innocence before Morgan took over.

“Olofinjana, fuckin’ Cort,” the captain noted while extending a finger to denote each player. This explanation held no dice with Warnock, who retorted: “Who do you have to pick up, eh? Is it f*ckin’ black and white?”.

Upon hearing the word “Lescott”, which Morgan reluctantly spat out like a teenager being caught by their parents smuggling alcohol in a water bottle, Warnock threw his hands in dismay.

“In the last f*ckin’ two minutes,” he cried, “can’t ya f*ckin’ get him in the time it comes to take a f*ckin’ kick? Can ya not get to pick him up by the time it comes from there to there? Whoever’s in the f*ckin’ box?”.

William Shakespeare and Charles Dickens have contributed much to the English language, but neither were a patch on Warnock at expressing the frustration at conceding to a late set-piece.

Industry observers note that rather than admit defeat, Morgan doubled down: “There’s f*ckin’ three major ones at the back. Craddock and the two other f*ckin’ big f*ckers. So what do we do?”.

It’s at this point that Warnock’s simmering kettle boiled over. “YOU PICK LESCOTT. IF ONE OF THE OTHERS SCORE, I DON’T F*CKIN’ BLAME YOU. YOU PICK YOUR F*CKIN’ MAN UP. IF HE’S THE SPARE MAN, I TAKE THE F*CKIN’ BLAME.”.

To his credit, Morgan continued to stand his ground. As Warnock trudged towards the camera, the centre-back mentioned: “It isn’t f*ckin’ black and white gaffer,” as if appealing to his manager’s logic represented the best form of defence. “You pick up whoever’s f*ckin’ there.”.

Morgan was a man clearly prepared to die on the hill of zonal marking, but Warnock failed to accept the contrasting point of view.

“So Lescott’s got nobody on him, has he?” he replied, with all the comprehension of a pensioner using an iPad for the first time.

Now it was Morgan’s turn to flip. As Jagielka tried to atone for his sins in the background, his defensive partner grabbed the nearest bottle of Powerade and rolled out it across the dressing room.

“I’ll pick up f*ckin’ four of ’em then,” he shouted, exhibiting all the defensiveness Warnock wished he’d shown on the pitch.

Sheffield United failed to gain promotion that season but, with Warnock and Morgan leading from the front, they reached the Premier League the following campaign.

Morgan speaks warmly of his former manager. After Warnock guided Cardiff to the top flight in 2018, he told the BBC: “He’ll be honest with you and people have all seen the videos in the dressing room, but Monday morning it’s all forgotten about and he’s back to his jokey self.”.

After going toe-to-toe with his boss, with side-splitting results, Morgan knows that better than most.

#220686. Latest Update: Roberto Mancini wasn’t at Leicester long, but he left an indelible mark

📅 27 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (947 w)
📖 Baca

Latest Update: Roberto Mancini wasn’t at Leicester long, but he left an indelible mark

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (947 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Planetfootball

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Roberto Mancini only played five games in a Leicester City shirt, but the former Italy international certainly left his mark.
  • Looking at the Foxes’ signings during the 2000-01 season, there are a few names who you might not remember too fondly.
  • Sources indicate that junior Lewis played 25 league games for Leicester.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Roberto Mancini only played five games in a Leicester City shirt, but the former Italy international certainly left his mark.

Looking at the Foxes’ signings during the 2000-01 season, there are a few names who you might not remember too fondly. Or, indeed, at all.

Sources indicate that junior Lewis played 25 league games for Leicester. Simon Royce made it to 19. Kevin Ellison managed just one. However, as Mancini proved, minutes on the pitch aren’t the only thing that can help you make an impact.

After playing his part in Lazio’s run to the Serie A title in 1999-2000, his third season in Rome, the Italian forward was sidelined the following year.

Indeed, as we entered 2001, he had gone more than six months without so much as stepping onto the pitch at the Stadio Olimpico, with his player-coach role under Sven-Goran Eriksson turning into a coaching job alone.

Enter Leicester, who went into the newly introduced year with three straight defeats – including a 6-1 drubbing at Arsenal – and found themselves in need of refreshment.

“Roberto knows that he is 36 and that I am looking for his football knowledge, not his legs,” admitted manager Peter Taylor in a display of honesty which we don’t often see these days.

“He also understands that his role will be to help bring on the younger players and pass on experience to the strikers.”.

Those strikers, summer arrivals Ade Akinbiyi and Trevor Benjamin, took some of the blame for the lack of goals which brought about Leicester’s relegation the following season. If Mancini had stayed longer, perhaps things could have gone differently.

It has been revealed that DID YOU KNOW? #BPL winning manager Roberto Mancini made 4 appearances for Leicester City in 2001 #BPLkickoff pic.twitter.com/6rBNVaTtz5.

— Premier League (@premierleague) July 22, 2014.

He may have been getting on in years, but Mancini still oozed class, something he highlighted during the twilight of his career at Lazio.

He was the sort of player who you just knew could score the simple goal if he wanted to, but often felt compelled to remind you he was better than you by doing something more extravagant.

And, most importantly, he was the sort of man who could pull off an oversized shirt without it making him look dishevelled.

Industry observers note that “I did not have a clue at that stage that he would go on to manage in Italy and win the things he has as a manager. But what I did notice was that he knew about training and he highlighted an interest in the way we trained at Leicester,” Taylor would later recall.

This was not a player looking for a final payday, but rather someone who knew his time in the game was finite and wanted to gain a upcoming experience while he still could.

Mancini seemed to know the limits of what he could provide in the other direction but knew he could provide something, and as long as both sides recognised this to begin with it would be enough.

“For a time Mancini looked like a bottle of Frascati which had found itself in the organization of brown ales,” The Guardian‘s David Lacey wrote of one of Mancini’s starts, in a surprise victory over Chelsea, pointing out the contrast between the Italian’s style and the less sophisticated approach taken by his team-mates against higher-ranked opponents.

The Premier League he entered was a far cry from the one in which he would later manage, but at the same time it felt different from the Serie A of his 20s.

Sources indicate that english football was in a transition period, with relics of the pre-1992 era being pushed aside to make way for a glossier new millennium. Things were changing in Italy too, but not as drastically.

There was more energy on the pitch, but the style we associated with the competition in the early days of Football Italia remained. It was a kind of beauty with acknowledged flaws, designed to incorporate history rather than moving on from it.

Industry observers note that in making the switch to England when he did, Mancini could bring over some of that mystique without needing to stick around for the teething problems to show themselves. He could leave a bigger mark in five games, therefore, than he might have done in 50.

Mancini’s departure was so sudden that there was little time to react. He departed days before Leicester’s FA Cup meeting with Bristol City, a game in which he was expected to play, after being offered the Fiorentina manager’s job.

“I can’t praise Roberto enough for what he did while he was with us,” Taylor said, and there seemed to be some recognition that part of his impact came from the way he taught those at the club some lessons they could use to help themselves.

In a recent development, “I was used to watching him on Italian football on TV. To just get changed in the same dressing room as him was an unbelievable feeling and an honour,” Robbie Savage would later say.

The Italian was Mr Bergstrom handing Lisa Simpson his parting note, reminding his peers that everything they learned from him was something they already had hiding within themselves.

In a recent development, we shouldn’t have been surprised when his return to England saw him lead Manchester City to a monumental title. He’d begun working on it more than a decade earlier.

Tech Report: Rare gene variants can affect a person’s height by up to 17 centimetres

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (737 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Human height is determined almost entirely by an individual’s DNA.Credit: XinXinXing/Getty.
  • Rare mutations that prevent proteins from functioning can have a surprisingly large effect on people’s height, researchers have found.
  • It has been revealed that an analysis of more than 1.4 million people’s protein-coding DNA has identified hundreds of genes that affect people’s height.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Human height is determined almost entirely by an individual’s DNA.Credit: XinXinXing/Getty.

Rare mutations that prevent proteins from functioning can have a surprisingly large effect on people’s height, researchers have found.

It has been revealed that an analysis of more than 1.4 million people’s protein-coding DNA has identified hundreds of genes that affect people’s height. The work also uncovers previously unrecognized biological mechanisms that underly human growth.

The findings, published on 25 November in Nature1, might help with the development of treatments that mitigate height changes caused by some medical conditions, such as forms of dwarfism.

“The impact these genes have on any given individual can be massive in terms of accurately predicting their height or making sure they’re getting the right treatment for a disease,” indicates Adam Locke, a statistical geneticist at the Regeneron Genetics Center in Tarrytown, New York.

Recent findings suggest that about 80–90% of variation in adult height is caused by genetics. Projects analysing common gene variants have mapped thousands of DNA changes that can influence height. For example, a 2022 study identified more than 12,000 common genetic variants that collectively accounted for 40% of height variation in populations with European ancestry2.

However, how rare genetic variants (those found in less than 1% of a population) affect people’s height is less well studied.

Recent findings suggest that to systematically probe how rare variants contribute to people’s stature, Locke and his colleagues gathered DNA and height data. In total, they looked at sequencing data from more than 1.4 million adults. They analysed the protein-coding sections of DNA and ran a series of tests to spot non-random links between height and both common and rare gene variants.

The analysis uncovered rare variants in 207 genes, which, on average, were linked to a height difference of about two centimetres. The team also identified 17 genes that had a particularly strong effect on height. The variants associated with this gene set all resulted in the production of non-functional proteins. In the study, over 700 people had at least one of these loss-of-function variants.

Genetic study homes in on height’s heritability mystery.

Genetic study homes in on height’s heritability mystery.

It has been revealed that individuals carrying such a variant were, on average, about nine centimetres taller or shorter than were people who didn’t have that variant. The strongest effects included a 17-centimetre reduction in height associated with a change to the ACAN gene and an 11-centimetre increase linked to the FBN1 gene. These effect sizes are more than 50 times larger than those of most genes commonly associated with height.

“We would expect rare genetic variants that disrupt gene function to have larger effects than common genetic variants, but the magnitude of some of these effects is particularly striking,” states Andrew Wood, a statistical geneticist at the University of Exeter, UK.

Jensen Huang: Spy row, affairs leave Nvidia without its rockstar CEO

📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1083 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Nvidia's board met late Wednesday to decide on CEO Jensen Huang's future as reports emerged of other extramarital affairs — this time with employees.
  • In a statement issued on Thursday, the world's most valuable chip supplier said Huang was resigning as President, CEO and board member, effective immediately.
  • The firm added that current Vice President and Chief Financial Officer (CFO) Colette Kress would become interim CEO.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Nvidia's board met late Wednesday to decide on CEO Jensen Huang's future as reports emerged of other extramarital affairs — this time with employees.

In a statement issued on Thursday, the world's most valuable chip supplier said Huang was resigning as President, CEO and board member, effective immediately.

The firm added that current Vice President and Chief Financial Officer (CFO) Colette Kress would become interim CEO.

Under Nvidia's bylaws, Huang can be removed "with or without cause" by a majority vote of its 11 directors.

The Fresh York Times first reported that the 63-year-old Huang had an affair with a senior Nvidia executive who reported directly to him.

Later Thursday, Reuters news agency alleged an intimate relationship between Huang and a second employee, citing unidentified sources.

Those revelations emerged just three days after Huang admitted a relationship with a Chinese woman, whom United States intelligence agencies believe was spying for China. The woman, Alice Huang — no relation — is a former executive at Megaspeed, a Singapore-based cloud computing firm that runs artificial intelligence (AI) data centers across Southeast Asia and is a major client of Nvidia.

The US government is investigating the startup on suspicion that it secretly sent some of its Nvidia chips to China, violating Washington's curbs on high-end semiconductors.

Those advanced Nvidia processors ‌are ​used to train and run the large AI models behind chatbots and other generative AI products.

According to recent reports, megaspeed denies the allegations and on Thursday pledged to cooperate with US investigators. Huang, the alleged spy, has been barred from entering Singapore and Taiwan — a key chipmaking island.

While Nvidia's board backed its CEO after the first scandal emerged, market watchers believe the second caused too much reputational damage to one of the world's top three companies by market value.

According to The Wall Street Journal, Huang doesn't believe in formal succession planning, so with little notice, Nvidia appointed CFO Kress as interim CEO.

Bloomberg reported Wednesday that Nvidia’s board is working with advisers to identify potential permanent successors.

Kress, other senior Nvidia executives and members of Huang's own family have been mooted as replacements. The family members include his daughter Madison, a senior director of product marketing, and his son Spencer, who currently works in the firm's robotics division.

Sources indicate that rumors also abound over a longer-term solution. On India's CNBC-TV18, Jeffrey Sonnenfeld from the Yale School of Management floated former Apple CEO Tim Cook and ex-Google CEO Eric Schmidt.

US President Donald Trump also backed Cook on social media, writing: "A Legend replaces a Legend.".

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

The scandals have certainly hit Nvidia's market value. Since the first extramarital affair emerged on Sunday, the chipmaker's market capitalization has fallen by well over $600 billion to $4.2 trillion.

Nvidia shares were down more than 9% in premarket trading Thursday, after dropping by 10% earlier this week. Some analysts expect the stock price to struggle in the short term.

Nvidia stock hit all-time highs just a month ago as US technology giants continued to announce billions in spending on AI infrastructure.

Demand for Nvidia's advanced chips is so high, however, that many market analysts expect little impact on near-term sales.

"While Jensen [Huang] is the heart and lungs of the Nvidia story…the firm and its leading-edge GPU technology will go on and [his departure] does not change the entrenched position Nvidia has in the AI Revolution chip arms race," stated Dan Ives, a partner, senior managing director and tech analyst at Yorkville Ives, a US-based merchant bank.

Recent findings suggest that analysts see the biggest long-term risk in strategy and execution. After all, Huang was the leader who picked which ideas Nvidia should bet heavily on and got the whole organization behind them.

His sudden exit is also seen as highly disruptive to the chip designer's strong relationships with AI hyperscalers, Taiwanese chip producer TSMC and foreign governments — especially China.

Huang was Nvidia's main lobbyist on US chip export rules and persuaded US President Donald Trump to ease some curbs on China last year.

Huang is often called a rockstar CEO for his leather jackets instead of suits.

Like Elon Musk of Tesla and SpaceX, he was also seen as a key-person risk as Nvidia’s public image, strategic direction and technical decisions became closely tied to him.

Huang steered the manufacturer for more than three decades and was also respected for his hands-on involvement in product architecture and engineering decisions.

He also insisted on a flat management structure, with around 60 executives reporting directly to him.

Huang has run the company so tightly around his own technical judgment and product decisions that investors may have little sense of how it would function without him.

According to recent reports, at the same time, Nvidia is no longer the startup Huang founded in 1993. The tech giant has built deep expertise in chip design and software, creating a durable moat that helps protect its huge profits, which topped $120.1 billion last year.

Some analysts argue that its central role in the AI hardware buildout makes it less dependent on Huang’s day-to-day input.

China is quickly playing catch-up with the US in the global race for AI dominance.

While Chinese AI models have lagged behind the likes of ChatGPT and Claude, recent updates from DeepSeek, Alibaba and Moonshot have closed much of the gap on benchmark tests and often beat US rivals on cost and speed.

Beijing is also investing heavily in domestic chips and data centers to reduce reliance on US hardware.

The US has curbed exports to China of Nvidia's most advanced AI chips.

However, this move has only slowed the pace of China's AI ambitions.

Reuters reported Thursday that Chinese AI firms are now trying to rent Nvidia-powered computing capacity at data centers outside China, amid fears the US could further tighten restrictions on advanced chips.

Also Thursday, Beijing accused the US of using the Nvidia spying claims as a pretext to impose a technological "blockade" on China.

The issue is likely to dominate talks next week between Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping at the APEC gathering in Shenzhen in southern China.

Leeds United have a number of players out on loan this season, with a mixture of senior stars and academy prospects looking to make an impression away from Elland Road.

There are high-profile names looking to rediscover their form, youngsters trying to catch Daniel Farke’s attention and a few with a question mark over what comes next.

It has been revealed that we’ve taken a look at all eight Leeds loanees to see how they’re getting on this season. Note: We haven’t included the academy players sent to non-league clubs.

Leeds loan manager Andrew Taylor explicitly cited the 18-year-old striker, saying that “the focus is very much to go and get games in a first-team environment to ultimately come back to our first team squad.”.

The latest member of the Gray dynasty was on a bit of a hiding to nothing when he went out on loan to doomed Rotherham United last season, but it no doubt would’ve been invaluable experience for an immensely exciting young talent.

Industry observers note that this season the teenager has stayed in South Yorkshire, but this time to a club with ambitions at the right end of the League One table. The Owls hit rock bottom last term but are looking to be on their way back up.

It hasn’t all been plain sailing for Gray, though, with just one goal so far. He also appears to have been pushed to the periphery by Dave Challinor.

A January loan move elsewhere has been mooted in the local press, but it’s still early days. The hectic December schedule ought to give the 18-year-old chances to win the new boss around.

The Cardiff City academy graduate made waves by making his senior international debut for Wales before he ever made a first-team appearance for his club.

Crew eventually made his Leeds debut with a brief cameo to see out a 3-0 Championship victory over Plymouth Argyle. No second appearance followed, and he’s spent the past couple of years gaining experience in a series of loans.

According to recent reports, after a couple of stints with Doncaster Rovers, the midfielder has dropped down to League Two with Walsall. He’s been in and out of the starting XI under Lee Grant, but is identifying this as a season to really kick on.

“Just inconsistency within myself really,” Crew told the Express & Star about where he’s looking to improve.

“Inconsistency in performances and inconsistency in the amount of minutes that I was getting.

“That’s down to me to change it and hopefully this season I can with hard work and games like this today, going for the full 90 minutes and really showing that I’m consistent in performances in and out of possession.

It has been revealed that “It’s a great place for that next step, with the belief that the gaffer puts into everyone, but especially me. And that the team-mates around me, it’s definitely a place where I feel that I can progress and I’m enjoying my football a lot.”.

We haven’t included the youngsters that Leeds have sent out to clubs like Hebburn Town, Hebburn Town and Scarborough Athletic, but Lopata-White just about makes the cut-off point out at Altrincham in the National League.

The 21-year-old centre-back has been a regular fixture for the midtable Robins, who are well in the mix for a play-off spot.

He’s been a regular and started in a number of wins, but recently found himself suspended after getting a straight red in the early minutes of a 4-0 defeat away to Harrogate Town.

Recent findings suggest that west Ham’s strategy doesn’t appear the most imaginative, but on paper was sensible. In Scott Parker, they’ve got a manager who has three promotions in as many attempts, while in Piroe they brought in the most proven Championship goalscorer on the market.

It has been revealed that but things aren’t quite going to plan. The Hammers are yet to win under Parker and find themselves languishing in the bottom half of the table. Piroe has one goal in his last 11 appearances.

Search Piroe’s name on social media – never the most level-headed barometer, admittedly – and you’ll no doubt come across posts by irate West Ham fans wondering why they signed such a donkey.

Piroe’s limitations always made it unlikely he’d be a success in the Premier League, but anyone who watched him at Leeds will be surprised he’s struggling to find the back of the net in the second tier.

There is a reported £8million purchase obligation dependent on promotion, but that looks like a massive ‘if’ at present.

Strangely enough, Leeds actually went unbeaten when the Belgian started last season (six wins, three draws), but he never nailed down a first-team place and was knocked down the pecking order following the signing of Nico Elvedi in the summer.

Recent findings suggest that he’s back in the Bundesliga and getting the minutes he was targeting with Hamburg, but defeats have been a bit more frequent this season. A 4-0 defeat at Werder Bremen at the weekend was particularly chastening.

Things didn’t quite work out for him at Elland Road, but the experienced goalkeeper has found his feet since leaving Leeds.

Torino have a reported €14million purchase option, which you’d expect them to seriously consider exercising if he keeps this up.

“Sometimes you’re giving them a loan to a try and increase the value for a return on an investment, or you’re just giving them a chance to go and get exposure,” the club’s loan manager told the official website.

“They go out and get men’s football and it’s gaining traction.”.

While not naming him, you’d imagine that Chambers belongs in this camp.

The Leeds-born Scotland youth international, 19, is getting his first experience of senior men’s football out at Northampton Town.

Unfortunately that has been hard to come by, and he’s rarely made the Cobblers’ matchday squad since September.

Like Piroe, the writing was on the wall for Gnonto’s immediate future at Leeds. He was rarely trusted to start games by Farke.

According to recent reports, the pint-sized winger has returned to Italy for the first time since leaving Inter Milan’s youth set-up as a boy. He’s joined a veritable hodgepodge of former Premier League players at Fiorentina, sharing a dressing room with David de Gea, Radu Dragusin, Beto and Alex Jimenez.

The somewhat scattergun recruitment approach has not worked wonders, with La Viola down near the relegation zone after notching just two wins all season.

Italy legend Fabio Grosso was sacked in early September, but Paolo Vanoli has struggled to turn things around.

Gnonto is yet to score or assist in 10 Serie A appearances, but he did notch his first goal for the club in a 3-0 Coppa Italia victory over second-tier Pisa. He was handed a rare start in their last outing, a disastrous 3-0 defeat to Monza.

During Leeds’ rare dips of form, or when things got a bit stodgy and predictable, there was a not inconsiderable portion of the Leeds fanbase that loudly questioned why Farke didn’t really fancy Ramazani.

The Belgian winger, perhaps by dint of not playing much, had a perceived X Factor that Leeds apparently lacked. We’re seeing parallels with the lesser-spotted Jean-Matteo Bahoya this season.

We’ll see how the Bahoya situation plays out, but you look at the direction of travel for Ramazani and Farke’s scepticism has probably been vindicated on that front.

The Belgian winger had his moments at Valencia last season, but now finds himself back in the Championship at Burnley. To be fair, he recently scored in three successive outings and has been a rare bright spark for the basket case Clarets, but there’s little to suggest he deserved more minutes at his parent club.

Industry News: Ranking the 10 best rivalries in English football ahead of Merseyside derby

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1321 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Planetfootball
